correctness.rationale: Positive edge weights reduce the sampled kernel to edge equations. Their signed cyclic recurrence has one free initial value exactly for an even cycle with equal products of fractions and complements; independent nodal values lift these traces. K plus the sampled penalty is positive definite because no nonzero constant is in the sampling kernel. Uniform boundedness and testing on the sampling kernel give convergence to the unique restricted stiffness solution. With resonance, a nonzero K-orthogonal complement to the zero-trace space gives a load annihilating the Dirichlet space but not that complement. For the unit-conductivity square, independently assembling in the tensor basis (1,1-2x,1-2y,f) gives diagonal stiffness (0,4,4,8/3) and load (0,0,0,1/9). Exact inversion gives the f coefficient as [eps^2 lambda^2+6 eps^2 lambda+2 lambda^2+8 lambda+8]/[6(3 eps^2 lambda^3+28 eps^2 lambda^2+60 eps^2 lambda+8 lambda^2+32 lambda+32)]. Dividing by lambda^2 gives 1/(24+9 tau) for every finite joint-limit sequence, including tau=0; the other three coefficients vanish. In the infinite-product regime the same quotient and transverse terms vanish (also det C=eps/4 and the simple defect yields sigma_min~|eps|/2 near zero). The integrated trace of f squared is 4/3 and reflection symmetry decouples f, giving the stated exact-integration coefficient. The own symbolic replay was /workspace/branches/independent-replays.py 2; frozen verify.py and recorded output claims were inspected, not executed. The numerical constant is for the assembled unit-conductivity, unit-weight square, not arbitrary stiffness or boundary weights.
